newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Card brings Singapore closer to cashless society.
newsitem.headline: Card brings Singapore closer to cashless society.

text.p: Singapore Finance Minister Richard Hu said on Tuesday the country was a step closer to becoming a cashless society with the launch of a new pre-paid electronic card.
Speaking at the official launch, Hu said the government's vision was for society to "dispense with the need to handle cash and cheques".
He said other electronic transaction systems introduced in Singapore over the past 10 years had brought substantial savings in handling costs.
The CashCard scheme uses the latest smartcard techology to store cash on a payment card. It is designed to be used for small-value purchases, such as payments at vending machines.
The card, which took five years and Singapore $40 million (US$28.57 million) to develop, is backed by a consortium of seven Singapore banks.
